title: Patriots’ Maye Dilemma, Chargers’ Collapse, Cowboys’ Fall: NFL Week 3 Sunday Takeaways
body:
The NFL’s third week has already produced a handful of storylines that could shape the rest of the season, from a rookie quarterback’s early struggles to a star tight end’s dramatic return from injury. New England’s first‑round pick Drake Maye tossed six interceptions in a loss that left the Patriots’ future at quarterback in doubt, while the Los Angeles Chargers slipped to a franchise‑worst 0‑3 start after a dismal showing against the Denver Broncos. Meanwhile, the Dallas Cowboys’ offense imploded in the second half against the Philadelphia Eagles, and San Francisco’s Brock Bowers dazzled in his first game back from knee surgery, hinting at a potent offensive weapon for the 49ers moving forward.

Maye’s three‑game rookie stretch has been a roller‑coaster, but the six picks in the Patriots’ 24‑17 defeat at the hands of the New York Jets underscore a deeper issue than simple inexperience. The 22‑year‑old showed flashes of arm strength and poise in the first half, completing 12 of 18 passes for 150 yards, but a series of misreads and forced throws in the second quarter resulted in three interceptions, two of which were returned for significant yardage. Veteran coach Bill Belichick, known for his willingness to make swift adjustments, faced a dilemma: protect the rookie’s development or demand immediate results. The Patriots’ offensive line, still grappling with injuries, gave Maye insufficient time, while the secondary’s aggressive coverage left the young quarterback with limited windows. As the Patriots look ahead to a Week 4 matchup with the Buffalo Bills, the coaching staff will likely simplify the playbook, rely more heavily on the running game, and perhaps consider a veteran backup to steady the ship.

Across the country, the Chargers’ slide to 0‑3 is a stark reminder that talent alone does not guarantee success. After a promising 2023 campaign, Los Angeles entered the season with high expectations, yet the 31‑10 loss to Denver exposed glaring deficiencies on both sides of the ball. Quarterback Justin Herbert, who has been a perennial MVP candidate, threw two interceptions and struggled to find rhythm against a disciplined Broncos defense that consistently pressured him. The offensive line allowed five sacks, and the defense surrendered 400 yards of total offense, including a 70‑yard touchdown run. The Chargers’ front office now faces pressure to address the line’s protection schemes and to re‑evaluate the defensive coordinator’s play‑calling, especially in third‑down situations. With a relatively favorable schedule looming, the team must find a way to halt the downward spiral before the playoff window closes.

The Cowboys, long‑favored to contend in the NFC East, were humbled by the Eagles in a game that turned into a second‑half shootout. After building a 14‑7 lead at halftime, Dallas’ offense stalled, committing three turnovers and failing to convert on critical third downs. Quarterback Dak Prescott, who has been praised for his leadership, threw two interceptions and was sacked four times, highlighting a lack of protection from an offensive line still reeling from injuries to key tackles. Moreover, the Cowboys’ once‑reliable running game was stifled by Philadelphia’s aggressive front seven, limiting Ezekiel Elliott to just 38 yards on 12 carries. The loss raises questions about the team’s depth and whether the coaching staff can adapt its scheme to a more balanced attack that doesn’t rely solely on Prescott’s arm.

In stark contrast, San Francisco’s Brock Bowers delivered a performance that could become a turning point for the 49ers’ offense. Returning after missing the first two weeks due to a meniscus repair, the 6‑4, 250‑pound tight end hauled in five catches for 73 yards and a touchdown, showcasing the same athleticism that made him a first‑round pick in 2022. His ability to line up in the slot, stretch the field, and create mismatches against linebackers gave head coach Kyle Shanahan a versatile weapon that can open up the run game for Christian McCaffrey. Bowers’ quick recovery also speaks to the advances in sports medicine and the 49ers’ commitment to player health. If he stays healthy, his presence could alleviate some of the pressure on the passing attack and provide a reliable red‑zone target.

Looking ahead, the NFL’s landscape remains fluid, with early-season turbulence offering both cautionary tales and hopeful signs. The Patriots must decide whether to nurture Maye’s raw talent or pivot to a more veteran‑centric approach, while the Chargers need to address fundamental protection and defensive lapses before the season’s midpoint.
